sph_interpretive_translation: A ruler must not summon those who are engaged in dharma for advancement, who depend on others while acting deceitfully, or who are intoxicated, insane, or heedless among his servants.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is invalidated when exercised over those aligned with dharma
Causation is disrupted by dependence rooted in deception
Capacity-based responsibility excludes states of intoxication or mental instability
Restoration logic demands exclusion of unfit agents from service
Consciousness alignment requires discernment between dharmic and adharmic presence
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent.is_dharmically_engaged AND action.is_advancement THEN ruler.authority = null
IF agent.is_deceitful AND agent.is_dependent_on_other THEN agent.eligibility_for_service = false
IF agent.state IN [intoxicated, insane, heedless] THEN agent.operational_capacity = false
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, summoning power must be denied to rulers or authorities attempting to involve dharmically active individuals whose alignment disrupts punitive frameworks. Fitness for service is assessed through consciousness-state mapping rather than procedural compliance alone.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies that summoning those unfit or dharmically oriented creates disorder. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how misaligned summoning leads to systemic collapse. Responsibility lies with the summoner to ensure capacity. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that exclusion restores order without inflicting suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Realign summoning protocols to exclude unqualified agents
Responsibility assumption protocol: Summoner must verify fitness prior to invocation
Capacity restoration: Intoxicated or unstable individuals undergo consciousness recalibration
Integrity reintegration: Dharmically engaged persons are returned to their natural function
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is restored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
